newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian housing recovery remains sluggish-REIA.
newsitem.headline: Australian housing recovery remains sluggish-REIA.

text.p: The housing recovery in Australia remains sluggish despite early hopes that lower interest rates would help to kick start employment and stronger economic growth, according to the Real Estate Institute of Australia.
Responding to Friday's release of May housing finance, which showed an 8.4 percent fall, REIA President Don Brindley said it reflected continuing consumer worries about the future.
"In the past, refinancing has boosted loan approvals with people exploiting falling interest rates. However, even refinancing fell 22.6 percent during May," Brindley said.

Brindley said the economy remains surprising unresponsive to lower interest rates and there is a clear call for confidence building measures with a structural unemployment problem dampening overall business activity.

"Flat population growth associated with cuts to immigration, also reduces opportunities for economic expansion. Business and consumer uncertainty must be addressed through policy measures not just interest rate cuts," Brindley said in a statement.

"REIA urges the government to work to liberate business initiative and promote a clear future vision through comprehensive tax reform, effective labour market programmes and the development of a national population policy," he added.
